sources.note: Nothing on accent, stress or tone. The only characterisations of the sound of the language are impressionistic: 'very gutteral in sound and extremely limited in power of expression' (p. 20) and 'very irregular and seems to me totally impossible to systematise' (p. 21); then numerals 1-5 and a c.75-item vocabulary in English amateur spelling without accent marks (Nannie earth, Ejugabah fire, Doongalla water, Ingin sun, Wurboonburra moon, Durgun rain.. sources.citation: AIATSIS AUSTLANG entry E61 Bindal (Internet Archive copy 2024-10-16 of collection.aiatsis.gov.au/austlang/language/e61)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Documentation table: Word list 'Less than 20 pages' (score 1), Text 0, Grammar 0, Audio-visual 0. Comment: 'The data for this language are scarce. Breen unpacks the historical confusion around two Lower Burdekin wordlists in Curr (1886, Vol 2: 488-491).. Breen concludes there are two different languages in these wordlists, both referred to as Bindal, and that neither language is a Mari dialect (2009:245).'

sources.citation: Breen, Gavan. 2009. The Biri dialects and their neighbours. Transactions of the Royal Society of South Australia 133(2): 219-256.
sources.note: The only modern linguistic treatment of the two Curr 'Lower Burdekin' wordlists (retranscription and classification, p.245); if anyone has said anything about Bindal phonology it is here, though a stress statement from 1886 spellings is unlikely.
